## Body

# #341 reviewer verdict at f7cf59e: BLOCK (one narrow finding)

## F001 (P1, normal-use regression): a daemon started under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR stops searching ~/.claude
`UdsTransport::new(pij_harnesses::claude_homes(), ..)` (crates/daemon/src/lib.rs:675). `claude_homes()` calls
`claude_homes_from(CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, HOME)` (claude_settings.rs:121-136): a set CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR REPLACES `$HOME/.claude`
(`else if`), and `configured_*` test at claude_settings.rs:1763 asserts exactly `[configured, .claude-alt]`. That rule is
intended for settings writes, but for the transport it is new: main hardcoded `$HOME/.claude/sessions` unconditionally.
`pij-rs daemon bounce` launches the daemon with the caller's env (crates/cli/src/bounce/mod.rs:294-308, no env_clear/env_remove),
and a Claude alt seat's shell carries CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-alt. So a bounce (or `just bounce-rs`) run from any cc-alt
seat yields homes = [~/.claude-alt] (+ alts.toml homes; this machine has none naming ~/.claude): every DEFAULT-home Claude seat
then misses its record and falls back to tmux typing, the mirror image of the bug this PR fixes. Not a misdelivery (brakes hold),
a silent degradation. Fix (small): the transport's list always includes `$HOME/.claude` (e.g. chain `claude_homes_from(None, HOME)`
into the list in lib.rs; `from_sessions_dirs` already dedupes by canonical path), plus a test that a configured CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
still searches `$HOME/.claude`. Also correct docs/how/pij-rs-api.md, which states `~/.claude` is always searched.

## Security (pass)
- pid+start identity is applied per home: the exact loop checks record.pid, observed.local == proc_start and (live_endpoint)
  observed.utc == recorded for EVERY dir; a stale/forged `<pid>.json` in another home with a different start is skipped. A record
  matching both pid and start names the same process, so no cross-seat steer.
- Pane fallback: every candidate must be live by its own pid's start; two live owners across homes return None (verified by mutant).
- Peer token comes from the SAME dir as the record (`matching_peer_token(dir, ..)`), never mixed across homes.
- messagingSocketPath is not validated (no owner/symlink check). Pre-existing on main, same-user trust boundary; not widened in kind.
- Homes come from the daemon's env, `~/.claude-alt` if it exists, and `~/.pij-rs/alts.toml` claude homes. No repo-local file can
  add one; a same-user seat that edits alts.toml already owns everything. Note for security role, not a finding.

## Correctness
- Order deterministic: homes in claude_homes() order; exact match is first valid home (only one process can match pid+start).
  Ambiguity is a refusal, not first-match.
- Homes are fixed at construction (boot). An alt home added to alts.toml later is searched only after a daemon bounce.

## Cost (confirmed)
Per Claude probe: up to one `<pid>.json` open per home, else one read_dir per home; plus the pre-existing one read_dir of the
matched home for its peer key (`matching_peer_token`, omitted from the PR's table, unchanged). One canonicalize per home at boot.
No launches, no per-tick or per-seat loop added; spawn_sites unaffected.

## Mutation (own, archive of HEAD, shared-build nice 19; baseline 34/34)
- M1 cross-home ambiguity `return None` -> `continue`: KILLED (two_live_owners_..._across_two_homes, two_live_pane_records_...).
- M2 dedupe removed: KILLED (one_home_named_twice_is_searched_once).
- M3 exact-pid loop first home only: KILLED (an_alt_home_seat_is_found_on_its_socket_by_pid_and_by_pane).
All by assertion, not compile failure. Temp archive removed.

## Privacy

## Follow-up (a) claude_bind.rs:168
Narrow: only daemon-SPAWNED pending Claude seats (spawn_id set, no proc) use it; a spawn through an alt names alt.home and is
handled. An alt-less seat lands in a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR home only when the daemon itself runs with that env, i.e. the same root
cause as F001. Worth proposing to Jordan together with F001 (one rule: which homes the daemon considers, independent of its own
env), not as a separate urgent bug.
